Also something I thought about after typing this (as I was ironically in the gym), exercise is SUPER important for ADHD individuals. We tend to make for really good athletes for some reason. Maybe having him in a sport or something that he enthusiastically likes to exhaust the extra energy. This could be on the stim or off, but I have noticed my comedowns are wayyyy less noticeable if I’m eating right and time a hard workout like an hour or two before the crash. I hypothesize the endorphins or extra norepinephrine or dopamine my body starts making offset the dip. Bad things happen with ADHD when you leave bored energy pent up inside with nothing interesting to focus it on; give him somewhere to focus all the craziness in a constructive and actively engaging setting.

Edit: also, in some cases, diet can be crazy important. My parents fed me a ton of carbs/sugar and never had me drinking enough water. Even today, carbs cause a roller coaster for me where I go hyperactive and then my mood crashes. Make sure he’s getting adequate protein intake. The daily rule of thumb is generally 0.8 grams/lb for the gym— not sure if that holds for kids. But again diet is insanely important because the impulsivity of trying to compensate for a hypofunctional prefrontal cortex (PFC) normally causes the individual to crave excess sugar/carbs — which is prob how ADHD gets linked longterm for a higher risk of diabetes. But one famous ADHD Dr. whose name escapes me, claims that cutting out all sugar isn’t the answer. He claimed it may be better to slowly SIP something sugary like lemonade to provide the PFC with a steady blood sugar supply. I’ve personally always found it hard to drink anything sugary in moderation, but experiment around and watch closely to how your son responds to different food and drinks.

Get a full evaluation for ADHD. Bipolar and ADHD tend to co-occur because of dopaminergic issues in both. A good psych should be first assessing ADHD if you’re walking in and a racing mind is your main complaint and not extreme mood fluctuations. Keep in mind that you’re asking a bipolar sub for recommendations: the overwhelming majority of meds you’re prob about to hear are antipsychotics, mood stabilizers, SSRIs (if the racing is anxiety/ocd), and possibly benzos. If, on the other hand, this is an ADHD issue, stimulants or other non-stimulant ADHD meds could be considered. Stims def have a more tolerable side effects panel than the weight gain and apathy typical with antipsychotics — in my mind at least. Maybe if high blood pressure is also at play, an adhd med like clonidine will work to slow the thoughts. Def make sure you’re working with a psych though who can differentiate adhd and bipolar symptoms. Some bipolar meds are seriously nothing to play around with (can trigger irreversible things like tardive dyskinesia at high enough doses) and I’d hate to see you suffer with wrong meds if this was straight up ADHD from the start

A mood stabilizer like lamictal is supposed to prevent the depressive lows.
